title: Earl Hines cuts his pay twice, so he gives notice
summary: Hines started him at $250, cut $25 in California and another $25 in Chicago; he gave notice at Snookie's to take the Porgy and Bess job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Milt in mind, and somebody else, you know. But when you got back here, when the show got back -- now we -- I'm still with Earl while this is going on, and what Earl is doing, he starts me out at a salary -- he started me out at 250.00. Well, I was happy because I liked to play with Earl and I liked his piano and everything, and I can make both ends meet then, you know. So now he comes up and he says, "Well, I'm going to have to cut you 25.00." So I said okay. I said it was kind of rough on me, and so and so, but I still like it. And now this makes me think more of the thing of "Porgy and Bess" thing, you know. And we were out in California then, so Benny Green comes in and he says, "Did you get a cut?" I said yeah, and he said, "I did too, you know." So what the heck, I said, it's still pretty good, you know. It's not bad.

So then, when we get to Chicago, he says, "I'm going to have to cut another 25.00." So I says, well, okay, what can I say, you know. Then we left Chicago, the Capital Lounge, and we're coming into Snookey's on 46th Street, and so "Porgy and Bess" is getting ready -- is back in town, they're getting ready to open, and so I gave my notice. I told him that 200.00 -- because things had started going up now, you know. I said, "$200.00, I can't make it on that with the taxes and things, and I've got a chance to go down here in a show where I can sit down here for awhile, I can rest."
